subject: Tier bridge + feature anchoring questions — HealthForge packaging
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@healthforge.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healthforge.com>; David Lee <david.lee@healthforge.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on tier bridge and feature bundling for upcoming renewal

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the overview last week. We are narrowing in on a path for our Q1 renewal and have two blocking questions before procurement will move forward:

1) We currently run the Compact tier but expect a sustained throughput bump in Jan — can you outline a clean "tier bridge" approach for a temporary uplift (2–3 months) that preserves our Compact feature set without triggering a full-tier reprice?

2) If we opt to add the Conversational Reranker and Private VPC connector as an add-on, how are those treated during a downgrade back to Compact (do we lose access or get prorated credits)?

Can you send a short plan we can share with finance & procurement? Ideally a sketch with timelines, cost delta, and any rollback guardrails.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of ML Ops
HealthForge
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@healthforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on tier bridge and feature bundling for upcoming renewal

Hi Marta — thanks, good questions. High-level answers below and attaching an initial playbook.

- Tier bridge: We can provision a temporary Throughput bucket for a fixed 12-week window while keeping your Compact feature entitlements intact. The billing is consumption-based for that window (flat uplift + token overage). After the window we can either: 1) automatically expire the bucket and route traffic back to Compact, or 2) convert to a permanent Throughput commit with pro-rated charges.

- Add-ons during downgrade: Add-ons are tied to entitlements, not tier. If you downgrade off the Throughput commit and keep the add-ons, you’ll keep access but overage protection will be limited; alternatively we can convert unconsumed committed capacity into credits that apply to add-on consumption for the remainder of the term. Detailed options are in the attachment.

Looping in Ben for pricing scenarios and Kimberly for migration/runbook details — Ben/Kim, would you take the lead on a concise price table + step-by-step rollback checklist?

I attached: HF_Migration_Playbook_v1.pdf (sketch)

Talk soon,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@healthforge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-10T10:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on tier bridge and feature bundling for upcoming renewal

Hi all — pricing attach and quick summary below. See pricing_schedule_HF.xlsx attached.

Summary pricing scenarios (12-week bridge):
- Scenario A (Transient burst): No commit, flat uplift of $6,500/week for reserved burst capacity + pay-as-you-go overage. Approx +9% ARR over the quarter.
- Scenario B (Light commit): 3-month committed bucket at 40% discount vs on-demand for the burst capacity. Upfront invoice, convertible to permanent commit with crediting. Approx +6% ARR if converted.
- Scenario C (Permanent upgrade): Convert now to Throughput commit — deepest unit price but non-refundable commit. We can apply a 12% limited-term commercial concession for HF-2027-112 if signed by 11/24.

Add-on handling on downgrade:
- Conversational Reranker: Remains enabled; we protect configuration for 30 days post-downgrade. Usage retained but overage billed at standard add-on rates.
- Private VPC connector: Customer-managed networking persists; we will bill for connector seats monthly. If you sunset the connector, we can credit unused connector pro-rata into a platform credit for 90 days.

Action requests: Marta — which scenarios should I model into a 12-week TCO spreadsheet for finance? Laura/Kim — I flagged the DocuSign lane for the concession (link below).

—Ben
Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@healthforge.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-11T09:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on tier bridge and feature bundling for upcoming renewal

Marta — quick migration checklist and rollback guardrails below. I pulled this from the attached playbook (mutual_action_plan.docx).

Migration runbook (high level):
1) Pre-window (2 weeks): smoke tests on staging, validate KV cache warm-up, confirm VPC connector firewall rules.
2) Switch day (0): spin Throughput bucket, route 10% live traffic for 4 hours, monitor p99 latency and error-rate.
3) Ramp (Days 1–7): 10 -> 50 -> 100% traffic with automated KB caching enabled; verify eval prompts show consistent outputs.
4) Stabilize (Weeks 2–12): daily cost/latency digest; weekly checkpoint calls.

Rollback guardrails: automated route fallback if p99 latency > 850ms or error-rate delta > 1.5x for 15 minutes; preserve add-on entitlements and snapshot configs before downgrade.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx (detailed tasks), HF_Migration_Playbook_v1.pdf (ops sketches)

If you confirm Scenario A or B, I’ll schedule a dry-run with infra (we recommend one dry-run in a non-peak window).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@healthforge.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-12T15:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on tier bridge and feature bundling for upcoming renewal

Laura / Ben / Kim — this is extremely helpful, thank you. Procurement asked us to choose between Scenario A (no commit) or B (light commit) by EOD Friday.

Action from HealthForge: we’ll sign Scenario B if Redwood can: 1) add the 12% concession to the light-commit price (to mirror the permanent upgrade concession) and 2) include a 30-day post-downgrade protection window for the Reranker configuration (in writing).

If you can send an updated pricing_schedule_HF.xlsx reflecting that concession and a 1-page MOU covering the protection window, we can route to procurement and DocuSign.

Best,
Marta
Head of ML Ops, HealthForge
